claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 has a reported hierarchical heterostructure featuring multilevel chemical fluctuations.

A hybrid multiscale ML model integrating high-resolution microstructural imaging with targeted first-principles and CALPHAD data can predict Young’s modulus, yield strength, and fracture toughness of hierarchical-heterostructured HfNbTiVAl10.
High-resolution image descriptors can capture the hierarchical interfaces and multilevel chemical fluctuations relevant to the predictions.
Simulation-derived thermophysical parameters complement the image descriptors in mediating mechanical-property predictions.
Directly embedding intrinsic microstructural heterogeneities in the ML model retains key physics governing mechanical responses.
Using microstructural information and a reduced simulation set bypasses the need for exhaustive high-fidelity simulations.
The hybrid model will reduce prediction errors for Young’s modulus, yield strength, and toughness by roughly 15% relative to traditional simulation-only methods.
The hybrid model will reduce computational demands by around 50% relative to traditional simulation-only methods.
Current standard methods rely on extensive first-principles and CALPHAD simulations.
Conventional ML models used in the baseline do not fully incorporate hierarchical structural details.
The model may lose reliability when evaluated on microstructures that differ substantially from its training samples.
The model may lose reliability at extreme temperatures or strain rates absent from its training data.
The magnitude of the accuracy and efficiency improvements may vary with sample variability and testing protocols.

contradictions.description: The boundary excludes unrepresented temperatures, strain rates, and microstructures from the claimed reliable domain, but deterioration outside those boundaries is nevertheless designated as a falsifying result. Out-of-domain failure cannot decisively refute an explicitly in-domain hypothesis.
